content:
Toileting is one of the most frequent transfers in the day. Painful hips and knees can make it hard.

This guide covers equipment and getting help. It is educational information, not a diagnosis or personal treatment plan.

Types of equipment

  • Toilet frames with armrests.
  • Raised toilet seats.
  • Grab rails.
  • Combined frame and seat units.

Getting the right fit

Heights matter. An occupational therapist can measure and advise.

How to get equipment

Ask your council for a needs assessment or OT referral. Small aids may be free.

Using it safely

  • Check it is stable.
  • Stand up using the arms, not a towel rail.
  • Keep the route to the toilet clear and lit at night.

When to get help

  • Call 999 for chest pain, trouble breathing, signs of a stroke, or a fall with a possible serious injury.
  • Get urgent advice the same day (NHS 111 or your GP) for sudden confusion, a sudden drop in mobility, or a hot, swollen joint with fever.
  • See your GP for a steady decline over weeks, unplanned weight loss or repeated falls.

Never stop or change a prescribed medicine yourself. Ask your GP or pharmacist for a review.

Common questions

Do I have to pay?

Some equipment is provided free after assessment.

Can I buy my own?

Yes, but an OT assessment helps.

Sources and further reading
